- [x] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Fixes the `TorchSampling` temperature-scaling precision bug in #7857.

`TorchSampling.filter_logits` divided logits by the temperature **in the input's dtype**. For BF16/FP16 logits that (a) loses precision in the scaled logit and shifts top-p nucleus membership at moderate temperatures, and (b) overflows FP16 at `temperature=0` (the divisor is floored to `MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=1e-6`, so `logits * 1e6` → `inf`). The fix promotes the working buffer to FP32 before the division and the nucleus filtering; the downstream softmax / log-softmax already ran in FP32, so this is the right dtype for both sampling and log-probs. The `temperature == 1.0` shortcut still preserves the input dtype.

`Tensor.to(dtype)` returns `self` when the dtype already matches, so promoting the buffer has to request the copy explicitly. Without `copy=True` the `div_` would mutate the caller's logits in place for an FP32 input — the framework default (`params_dtype` defaults to `torch.float32`). The static batching path hands the sampler a **view** of the model's logits (`logits[:, -1, :]`), so the mutation would write the temperature-scaled and top-k/top-p-masked values back into that buffer, and the prompt log-probs computed from it afterwards (`F.log_softmax(logits, dim=2)`) would come out as `-inf` for every token outside the nucleus. `filter_logits` documents *"Returns a new tensor (input unmodified)"*; `copy=True` keeps that contract.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: Fixes #7857

## The failure

![BF16 nucleus shift and FP16 overflow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muditagrawal2007/Megatron-LM/issue-7857-figures/fig1_precision.png)

The issue's own numbers (Nemotron-H-8B-Base-8K, generated-token index 29, seed 123, `temperature=0.1`, `top_p=0.9`):

| Candidate | raw logit | BF16 scaled logit | probability (pre-fix) | probability (fixed) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `" to"` (1317) | 26.625 | 266 | 0.88079703 | 0.92414182 |
| `" over"` (2136) | 26.375 | 264 | 0.11920292 | 0.07585818 |

The leading token needs a probability above `top_p = 0.9` for the nucleus to stay a single token. BF16 rounding of the divisor (`26.625 / 0.1 = 266.25` → `266`) drops it to `0.8808`, so the runner-up survives the filter and the engine emits `2136` where the FP32 reference emits `1317` with the same prefix and RNG state.

The second failure is the issue's FP16 column: at `temperature = 0` the divisor is floored to `1e-6`, so `30.0 / 1e-6 = 3e7` overflows FP16 (max 65504) to `inf`, the softmax returns `NaN`, and the sampler emitted token `0` instead of the greedy token.

![Divergence map over temperature and logit gap](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/muditagrawal2007/Megatron-LM/issue-7857-figures/fig2_disagreement.png)

Left: the BF16 divisor quantizes the scaled gap, so the runner-up keeps ~12% of the mass until the raw gap passes `0.31`, while the FP32 reference drops it above `0.23` — the shaded band is where the two paths disagree. Right: how often the pre-fix path can emit a token the FP32 reference excludes; the issue's operating point (`temperature=0.1`, gap `0.25`) is marked.

Both figures are generated by `make_figures.py` in the [evidence branch](https://github.com/muditagrawal2007/Megatron-LM/tree/issue-7857-figures); it reproduces the pre-fix `filter_logits` and the fixed one side by side.

## Root cause

```python
# before
last_token_logits = last_token_logits.clone()
if temperature != 1.0:
    last_token_logits.div_(max(temperature, MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE))
```

`Tensor.div_(scalar)` runs in the tensor's own dtype, so the scaled logit is rounded to BF16/FP16 **before** the nucleus filter sees it.

## The fix

```python
# after
if temperature != 1.0:
    last_token_logits = last_token_logits.to(torch.float32, copy=True)
    last_token_logits.div_(max(temperature, MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE))
else:
    last_token_logits = last_token_logits.clone()
```

The divisor and the nucleus filter now run in FP32, so the scaled logits are the FP32 ones and the top-p boundary matches the reference exactly. At `temperature == 1.0` there is no division, so the input dtype is preserved and the extra FP32 copy is skipped.

`filter_logits` is shared with `log_probs_kernel`, so the processed log-probs now match the distribution that was actually sampled.

## Code provenance

No code was copied or adapted from an external source. The change is an independent implementation in the repository's own idiom; the `copy=True` promotion follows the existing `Tensor.to(..., copy=True)` usage in `megatron/core/optimizer/optimizer.py`.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [x] I have added relevant functional tests — not applicable: this is a sampling-precision fix in the inference path with no training-loop behavior change and no golden values.
- [x] If this PR adds or changes a GPU kernel (Triton, `jit_fuser`/`torch.compile`, CUDA extension, TE or external-library dispatch, or a scatter/index accumulation), I have added or updated its bit-exact determinism test and registered it in `tests/unit_tests/determinism/kernels/manifest.py` — not applicable: no kernel was added or changed. `filter_logits` is pure PyTorch, and the FlashInfer path is untouched.
- [x] I have added proper typing to my code — no new public API; `filter_logits` keeps its existing signature and annotations.
- [x] I have added relevant documentation — the `filter_logits` docstring now states the dtype contract (FP32 when the divisor runs, the input dtype otherwise) and the inline comment records the `copy=True` requirement and why it exists.
- [x] I have run the [autoformatter.sh](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/blob/main/tools/autoformat.sh) on my PR — `black`, `isort`, `ruff` and `pylint` (10.00/10) are clean on the changed files.

### Tests

`tests/unit_tests/inference/sampling/test_torch_sampling.py` — 53 tests pass (CPU only, no GPU needed):

Filter level:

- the issue's exact BF16 reproducer (leading token kept, runner-up masked) for both BF16 and FP16 inputs;
- FP16 does not overflow at `temperature=0`;
- the fixed path matches the FP32 reference (mask agreement plus finite-entry value match) across temperatures and top-p values;
- `filter_logits` returns FP32 for `temperature != 1.0` and preserves the input dtype for `temperature == 1.0`;
- `filter_logits` leaves the caller's logits untouched — for BF16/FP16/FP32 inputs, across temperatures, through a **view** of the input, and for `sample_from_logits`.

Sampler level (what a user observes):

- `test_bf16_sampler_never_emits_outside_the_fp32_nucleus` — over 64 seeds the sampler never draws a token the FP32 reference excludes. Against the pre-fix code the runner-up was drawn in 10 of those 64 seeds;
- `test_fp16_zero_temperature_emits_the_argmax` — at `temperature=0` the probabilities stay finite and the sampler agrees with greedy (the pre-fix code returned `NaN` probabilities and emitted token `0`).

`tests/unit_tests/inference/text_generation_controllers/test_text_generation_controller.py` — two new tests assert that the controller's `sample_from_logits` leaves the caller's logits (and a view of them) untouched.

**Verification.** The new tests were confirmed to **fail against the pre-fix code**: running the same test file against the base commit's `torch_sampling.py` fails 8 of them (the six filter-level regressions and both sampler-level ones), and all 53 pass with the fix. The controller tests need a GPU and run in CI.

Two pre-existing issues in the test files are also corrected here:

- `torch.testing.assert_equal` does not exist (`torch.testing` exposes `assert_close`, `assert_allclose`, `make_tensor`, `FileCheck`), so the non-mutation assertion added for this fix raised `AttributeError` instead of checking anything. Replaced with `torch.equal`.
- `test_sample_from_logits` divided a **view** of the caller's logits in place (`l.div_(temperature)`), corrupting its own fixture and causing a hidden double division. Made out-of-place.

### Manual verification of the end-to-end effect

Replaying the static batching sequence (`logits[:, -1, :]` → sample → `F.log_softmax(logits, dim=2)`) on FP32 logits, with the top-p filter applied:

| `filter_logits` variant | caller's logit buffer | prompt log-probs |
|---|---|---|
| released code (clone + in-dtype `div_`) | not mutated | exact |
| FP32 promotion without `copy=True` | **mutated** | `-inf` for every token outside the nucleus |
| this PR (FP32 + `copy=True`) | not mutated | exact |

The middle row is the hazard the `copy=True` avoids: the released code cloned the logits first, so it never mutated the caller, and neither does this PR.

## Notes for reviewers

- The FlashInfer sampling path is untouched. It already pins the invariant this PR establishes for TorchSampling (`scaled.dtype == torch.float32`, `flashinfer_sampling.py:104`).
- The dynamic engine reads the same `_all_logits_cuda` buffer for both sampling and log-probs, but survives today only because both paths copy their rows out via advanced indexing (`torch_sampling.py:233`, `torch_sampling.py:324`). This PR removes the reliance on that being incidental, but does not change the dynamic path's behavior.
- `temperature == 1.0` still returns the caller's dtype (unchanged behavior), while the divisor path returns FP32. Downstream `softmax`/`log_softmax` promote to FP32 either way.
- Performance: for BF16/FP16 inputs the filter now allocates an FP32 working buffer instead of a BF16/FP16 one, and the top-p sort runs over FP32. That is the same trade-off the FlashInfer backend already makes (it also scales into FP32), and it only applies to the `temperature != 1.0` path.
- Out of scope: the issue also asks whether the direct core APIs should normalize `temperature = 0` to greedy the way the HTTP endpoints do. That is an API-behaviour decision and is not touched here — this PR only removes the precision loss.

@@ -79,3 +79,284 @@ def test_low_precision_logits_do_not_collapse_tail_precision(self):
         # to compute in fp32.
         downcast_roundtrip = log_probs.to(torch.bfloat16).to(torch.float32)
         assert not torch.equal(log_probs, downcast_roundtrip)
+
+
+class TestFilterLogitsTemperaturePrecision:
+    """Regression tests for ``TorchSampling.filter_logits`` (issue #7857).
+
+    ``Tensor.div_(scalar)`` runs in the tensor's dtype. For BF16/FP16 inputs
+    that (a) loses precision in the scaled logit and shifts top-p nucleus
+    membership at moderate temperatures like 0.1, and (b) can overflow FP16
+    at temperature=0 (floored to MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=1e-6). The fix
+    promotes the working buffer to FP32 when scaling; the filters below run
+    on FP32 and the downstream softmax already runs in FP32.
+    """
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("input_dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+    def test_temperature_scaling_does_not_shift_top_p_nucleus(self, input_dtype):
+        """REGRESSION (issue #7857, BF16 column): with the BF16-divisor bug,
+        BF16 rounding of 26.625 / 0.1 = 266.25 -> 266 (loss of 0.25) makes
+        the BF16 gap between leading and runner-up 2.0 vs the FP32 gap 2.5,
+        raising the runner-up's softmax mass enough that top-p=0.9 retains
+        it where the FP32 reference masks it. The fix must reproduce the
+        FP32-reference filter."""
+        # Issue #7857 reproducer inputs: leading and runner-up logits that
+        # differ by 0.25 in BF16 / 0.5 in FP16 -- small enough that divisor
+        # rounding matters.
+        leading = 26.625 if input_dtype is torch.bfloat16 else 26.5
+        runner_up = 26.375 if input_dtype is torch.bfloat16 else 26.0
+        logits = torch.tensor([[leading, runner_up] + [-100.0] * 126], dtype=input_dtype)
+
+        filtered = TorchSampling.filter_logits(logits, temperature=0.1, top_k=0, top_p=0.9)
+
+        # The leading token must be retained (not masked to -inf).
+        assert filtered[0, 0] != float("-inf"), (
+            "leading token unexpectedly masked out -- top-p nucleus should " "always include it"
+        )
+        # The runner-up must be masked (-inf). The pre-fix BF16 path used to
+        # retain it because the BF16-rounded divisor (266, 264) inflated its
+        # softmax mass past the top-p cutoff.

+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("input_dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16])
+    def test_temperature_scaling_matches_fp32_reference(self, input_dtype):
+        """The fixed filter must match the FP32-computed reference for
+        BF16/FP16 inputs across the temperatures and top-p values that
+        exercise the divisor rounding path."""
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        vocab_size = 128
+        logits = torch.randn(4, vocab_size, dtype=input_dtype)
+
+        for temperature, top_p in (
+            (0.1, 0.0),
+            (0.1, 0.5),
+            (0.1, 0.9),
+            (0.5, 0.9),
+            (0.7, 0.5),
+            (1.5, 0.5),  # temperature > 1 also exercises the divisor path
+        ):
+            low_prec = TorchSampling.filter_logits(
+                logits, temperature=temperature, top_k=0, top_p=top_p
+            )
+            fp32_ref = TorchSampling.filter_logits(
+                logits.float(), temperature=temperature, top_k=0, top_p=top_p
+            )
+            # The mask must agree exactly: any divergence means the BF16/
+            # FP16 divisor truncation shifted the nucleus boundary.
+            low_prec_mask = torch.isinf(low_prec)
+            fp32_ref_mask = torch.isinf(fp32_ref)
+            assert torch.equal(low_prec_mask, fp32_ref_mask), (
+                f"{input_dtype} filter mask diverged from the FP32 reference "
+                f"at temperature={temperature}, top_p={top_p}: "
+                f"{int((low_prec_mask != fp32_ref_mask).sum())} entries differ"
+            )
+            # Finite entries should match within FP32 precision.
+            finite = ~low_prec_mask
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                low_prec[finite],
+                fp32_ref[finite],
+                msg=(
+                    f"{input_dtype} filter_logits diverged from the FP32 "
+                    f"reference at temperature={temperature}, top_p={top_p}"
+                ),
+            )

+    def test_fp16_does_not_overflow_at_zero_temperature(self):

+        divisor is floored to MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=1e-6, so
+        ``logits / 1e-6 = logits * 1e6`` overflows FP16 (max ~65504).
+        Scaling in FP32 keeps the result finite and the top-p mask valid."""
+        logits = torch.tensor([[30.0, 29.0, 28.0] + [-100.0] * 125], dtype=torch.float16)
+
+        filtered = TorchSampling.filter_logits(logits, temperature=0.0, top_k=0, top_p=0.9)
+
+        kept = filtered[0][filtered[0] != float("-inf")]
+        assert torch.isfinite(kept).all(), (
+            "FP16 logits overflowed to inf during temperature scaling at "
+            "temperature=0 (issue #7857)."
+        )
+        # Sanity: the leading token survives the top-p=0.9 filter.
+        assert filtered[0, 0] != float("-inf")

issue_comments.body:
This pull request requires additional validation before any workflows can run on NVIDIA's runners.

Pull request vetters can view their responsibilities [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/vetters).

Contributors can view more details about this message [here](https://docs.gha-runners.nvidia.com/cpr/contributors).

Added a second commit that closes the loop on this fix, and refreshed the description with the evidence figures.

**What the new commit adds** (`test(inference): pin the sampler-level symptoms of issue #7857`):

- `test_bf16_sampler_never_emits_outside_the_fp32_nucleus` — over 64 seeds the sampler never draws a token the FP32 reference excludes. Against the pre-fix code the runner-up was drawn in 10 of those 64 seeds, so this fails on the base commit and passes here.
- `test_fp16_zero_temperature_emits_the_argmax` — at `temperature=0` the probabilities stay finite and the sampler agrees with greedy. The pre-fix code returned `NaN` probabilities and emitted token `0` (the issue's `1124` vs `0` symptom).
- The `filter_logits` docstring now states the dtype contract: FP32 when the divisor runs (`temperature != 1.0`), the input dtype otherwise.

**Verification** — the same test file against the base commit's `torch_sampling.py` fails 8 of the new tests (6 filter-level + the 2 sampler-level ones above); all 53 pass with the fix.

**Figures** — the description now embeds two generated figures (the issue's numbers side by side, and a map of where the pre-fix path can diverge). They are regenerated by `make_figures.py` in the [evidence branch](https://github.com/muditagrawal2007/Megatron-LM/tree/issue-7857-figures), which also contains the script that reproduces the pre-fix `filter_logits`.

One correction to the previous description: the released code never mutated the caller's logits (the `clone()` came first) — the in-place mutation was what the FP32 promotion would have introduced without `copy=True`. The table in the description now labels the three variants accordingly.
